reason: E2 shows TiO precipitates form in a refractory HEA and contribute to strengthening, but it is a different alloy (NbMoTaWVTi) processed by MA and SPS, not TiVNbTa, and the strengthening is demonstrated at room temperature, not 1273 K. E1 discusses TiVNb but only addresses cracking resistance and weak temperature dependence of strength, with no mention of oxide precipitates or oxygen addition. Thus, the key premises about in situ oxide formation, high-temperature precipitation strengthening, and retained ductility in TiVNbTa are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Nanoscale Ti-rich oxide precipitates can form in situ in refractory HEAs with controlled oxygen addition
Such precipitates provide precipitation strengthening by impeding dislocations and pinning grain boundaries at high temperature
This strengthening mechanism can counteract thermal softening in TiVNbTa at 1273 K
The modified alloy will retain adequate ductility for the interlayer application
